content.readme:
Kernarium
===

Run a real Linux kernel natively on iOS, through the magic of [User-mode Linux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User-mode_Linux).

## Apps

### Andarium

The app was released on App Store but removed by Apple later due to violation of App Review Guidelines:
```
Guideline 2.5.2 & 1.1 - Performance - Software Requirements


We noticed that the app includes functionality that isn’t focused on the experience for supported Apple platforms.


Specifically, your app allows users to replicate Android operating systems on iOS platforms.
```

An Android emulator app built on the Kernarium runtime is **no longer** available for download in App Store. Source code is available under [`Andarium/`](/Andarium/).

#### Sideloading

You can sideload the app with [AltStore](https://altstore.io) or [SideStore](https://sidestore.io).

The easy way is to add the source, so updates show up in AltStore or SideStore:

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/imxieyi/Kernarium/main/sideload/source.json
```

Alternatively, install the IPA from [releases](https://github.com/imxieyi/Kernarium/releases) by hand:

1. Download `Andarium-<version>.ipa` on the device. It's about 1 GB.
2. Open AltStore or SideStore, tap `+` in **My Apps** and pick the IPA.

A few things to know:

- iOS 26 or later is required.
- A free Apple ID works, but the app expires after 7 days and must be refreshed in AltStore or SideStore.
- With a free Apple ID, Android gets less memory. AltStore 2.2 or later keeps the increased memory limit, SideStore doesn't by default. Extended virtual addressing needs a paid developer account.
- JIT is optional. To use it, assign the universal script to Andarium in StikDebug once, then open Andarium from StikDebug.
- To update by hand, install the new IPA with the same Apple ID and the same tool. It replaces the old version and keeps your virtual machine.

### Kernarium

A generic Linux emulator app capable of running various Linux distributions. It's still at an early stage of development and isn't ready for release yet. Source code is available under [`Kernarium/`](/Kernarium/).

## Overview

The User-mode Linux kernel is compiled to native arm64 code, then linked to an iOS runtime framework. The kernel runs natively without emulation. Userspace programs are emulated using an [iSH](https://github.com/ish-app/ish)-style threaded interpreter, with SMP support. Guest GPU acceleration is provided by [KosmicKrisp](https://docs.mesa3d.org/drivers/kosmickrisp.html), a translation layer from Vulkan to Metal.

This emulator architecture sits between a full system emulator (like [UTM](https://github.com/utmapp/UTM)) and a full userspace emulator (like [iSH](https://github.com/ish-app/ish)). It combines the benefits of a real Linux kernel and a userspace emulator that only needs to emulate userspace code. It's capable of running advanced workloads including Docker containers, Linux desktops, Wine/Proton and a full Android system at decent speed on modern iOS devices.

## Features

- Kernel
    - Mainline 6.18 LTS kernel for both Linux and Android guests
    - Supports most kernel features, including namespaces, SELinux and more
- CPU emulation
    - Supports `arm64`, `arm32`, `x86_64` guest instructions
    - Both interpreter and JIT execution modes
- GPU acceleration
    - Vulkan 1.4 via [KosmicKrisp](https://docs.mesa3d.org/drivers/kosmickrisp.html)
    - OpenGL 4.6 & GLES 3.2 via [Zink](https://docs.mesa3d.org/drivers/zink.html)
    - Hardware video encoding and decoding (H.264, HEVC; VP9 decoding) via [VideoToolbox](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/videotoolbox)
- Storage
    - Supports virtual disks via UBD driver, with discard support
    - Supports any Linux filesystem including ext2/3/4, erofs, xfs, ...
    - Supports loop devices and FUSE
- Network
    - Full Linux networking stack
    - Guest network access via [libslirp](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/slirp/libslirp)

## Build or Embed

Point your coding agent at this repo if you want to build the project or embed its runtime in other apps. The agent guide is [`AGENTS.md`](/AGENTS.md), and the documentation is under [`docs/`](/docs/).

Building Android system image requires a powerful remote x86_64 Linux building machine ([requirements](https://source.android.com/docs/setup/start/requirements)). Alternatively, you can download prebuilt images from [releases](https://github.com/imxieyi/Kernarium/releases) and point your coding agent at it.

## License

This project is licensed under GPL-2.0-or-later, except where a file's SPDX header says otherwise; see [`LICENSES/`](/LICENSES/).

# GTA: Vice City Stories — Native PC port (PS2 static recompilation)

A native **Windows and Linux** port of **Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories** (PS2, USA, SLUS-21590), made by
recompiling the game's PS2 executable into C++. Both are built from the same source and run natively: Direct3D 11 on
Windows, Vulkan on Linux.

**This repository contains no game code or game data.** You need your own copy of the game as an `.iso`.
The build reads the executable from your disc, and the finished game reads everything else from it while it runs.

Status: in development. See [docs/PROGRESS.md](docs/PROGRESS.md) for what works, and [docs/LINUX.md](docs/LINUX.md)
for the Linux build in detail.

## Install on Windows: the launcher (easiest)

1. Download the newest `VCS-Recomp-<version>-windows.zip` from the [Releases](../../releases) page and extract it
   somewhere short and local, like `C:\Games\VCS` (not Program Files, not a OneDrive-synced folder such as Desktop or
   Documents: the build writes thousands of files).
2. Start **`VCSLauncher.exe`** in that folder. It walks you through four steps, one at a time, then shows a big
   **Play** button:
   - **Folder**: the game is built in `build\` next to the launcher, or in a folder you choose (another drive with
     more room, say): *Choose another folder* on this step.
   - **Disc**: it looks for your `.iso` in Downloads, Desktop, Documents and its own folder; otherwise choose it (or
     drag it onto the window, or copy your disc from a DVD drive). It checks that it is the USA release.
   - **Build tools**: the game is compiled on your PC with Microsoft's free C++ tools. If they are missing,
     *Install build tools* runs Microsoft's installer with the right options (about 6 GB; Windows asks for permission).
   - **Build**: recompiles the game from your disc and compiles it, with a progress bar - 20 to 60 minutes the first
     time, a few minutes after an update. Nothing is downloaded during the build: the release brings Python and the
     libraries.
   - **Play**.

The launcher also backs up and restores your saves, makes a desktop shortcut, checks for a new release (only when you
ask, or at start if you turn that on in *Settings*), and zips the logs into a report for bug reports. Windows may warn
that the launcher is from an unknown publisher (it isn't signed): *More info > Run anyway*. How it works:
[docs/LAUNCHER.md](docs/LAUNCHER.md). Everything it does is a script in `tools/` you can also run yourself (below).
If the *Pricedown* font (GTA's lettering, free for personal desktop use from Typodermic) is installed on your PC, the
launcher uses it for its title and Play button; its licence doesn't allow including it, so it isn't.

   any 64-bit desktop with glibc 2.35 or newer: Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Linux Mint 21, Fedora, Arch and later, on
   X11 or Wayland. It needs a Vulkan driver (Mesa or NVIDIA's) and `python3`, which every desktop has.
2. Make it executable and start it: in the file manager, *Properties > Permissions > Allow executing as a program*, or
   `chmod +x VCS-Recomp-*.AppImage && ./VCS-Recomp-*.AppImage`. The first start puts the game's files (the source,
   the scripts, the libraries) in `~/.local/share/VCSRecomp/install`, where the game is built, then walks you through
   the same steps as on Windows:

   - **Disc**: your `.iso` from Downloads, Desktop or Documents, chosen, or dropped onto the window.
   - **Build tools**: the compiler (clang 19 or newer) and the libraries the build needs, from your distribution.

# FNV decompilation

The decompilation of FNV, the Steam release for PC (version 1.4.0.525): C++ source code rebuilt function by function
from the game's executable. Built with the compilers the game was built with, every function listed in
`build/units.json` compiles to the same bytes as the original.

The project was spearheaded on [fnvdecomp.com](https://fnvdecomp.com), where a frozen version of the community
project stays online.

- **What it is for.** The modding community has kept working on FNV for more than a decade. This repository is meant
  for that community: for research, modding and game preservation.
- **Not a way around buying the game.** It is not meant to replace owning the game and must not be used to play or
  share it without a copy of your own.
- **Source code only.** It contains no game files, no assets, no executables and nothing you can play, and nothing
  of the game is distributed here.
- **You need the game.** To use any of this you need to own the Steam version of FNV (1.4.0.525).
- **Public domain (CC0).** The contributors' own work here is dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0: use it as
  you see fit. That covers only what the contributors wrote, never the game itself; see [Legal](#legal).
- **Trademarks** belong to their holders, listed under [Legal](#legal). This project is not affiliated with or
  endorsed by any of them.

## Contributing

Pull requests are welcome from anyone. Most of what is left is readability: many functions still have placeholder
names (`FUN_00xxxxxx`), vague names or no comment, and all of that can be improved without changing a single byte of
the output. By opening a pull request you dedicate your contribution to the public domain under CC0 1.0, like the rest
of the contributors' work here (see [Legal](#legal)).

### The automatic check

Every pull request gets an automatic check, called `match`. It runs on GitHub's machines, involves no part of the
game, and has to pass before a pull request can be merged:

1. It finds the translation units your change can affect: the files you changed, every unit that includes them, and
   every unit whose entry in `build/units.json` changed.
2. It builds each of those units twice, from `main` and with your change, with the Microsoft compilers the game was
   built with.
3. Every function has to come out identical, at its original address: the same code bytes, and every call and data
   reference resolving to the same original address through `build/units.json`, exception-handling code included.
   A function that moved to another unit is compared with what it compiled to in its old unit. `main` matches the
   game byte for byte, so a change that passes still does.

What to expect:

- **Passes:** renaming functions, parameters, variables, types and fields; adding or improving comments;
  reformatting; restructuring headers and types; moving functions between units (see "Changing the build recipe"). A
  change only to comments, spacing or blank lines passes without a build.
- **Fails:** anything that changes what a function compiles to. The check lists the functions that differ by
  address; see what differs with your own copy of the game:
  `python3 tools/build_and_match.py --image <your FalloutNV.exe> --only <unit>`.
- **Needs a maintainer:** changes outside `src/`, `include/`, `build/units.json` and Markdown files (the tools, the
  workflow), and changes to `build/units.json` beyond what "Changing the build recipe" allows. The check fails on
  these and nobody can merge them, so open an issue instead. Changes to the tools, the workflow and `LICENSE` are made
  by the repository owner; tool changes are verified against the game.

### Review and merging

A pull request is merged when the check passes and two reviewers have approved it:

- Nobody can skip the check, the repository owner included.
- Two approvals are needed. An approval is dropped when new commits arrive, and the last push has to be approved by
  someone other than the person who made it.
- The pull request has to be up to date with `main`. If `main` moves first, use "Update branch" and the check runs
  again on the combined code.

After every change to `main`, the whole of `main` is also built against the game's executable on the project's own
machine. That build proves `main` still matches the game byte for byte, not only that it compiles the same as
before.

### Renaming a function

`build/units.json` lists every function by its original address and its decorated (mangled) name. When you rename a
function, put its new decorated name at the same address, in every unit that lists it; otherwise the check reports
the old name as unbound. Adding a declaration or a string literal can renumber the compiler's string labels
(`$SG...`) that `build/units.json` names; the check says so when that is the cause.

content.readme:
Atrium Desktop

不仅仅是桌面美化。
保留 Windows 的用法，换上一块实时折射的液态玻璃，
再用同一套设计语言，把任务栏、开始菜单、控制中心、通知和小组件连成一个整体。

下载  ·  功能  ·  开始使用  ·  English

## 不仅仅是桌面美化 Windows 的桌面是几代设计叠起来的：任务栏、托盘、开始菜单、通知、快捷设置，各有各的圆角、字号和动画。Atrium 把每天看到的这一层重新做了一遍，但没有改变你用 Windows 的方式。 - **用法不变**：固定应用、切换窗口、右键菜单、把文件拖到应用图标上打开，都和原来一样。 - **同一块玻璃**：栏、面板、菜单、通知和小组件用的是同一种材质，实时映出背后的桌面。 - **同一套设计语言**：圆角、间距、字体和动画遵循同一套规则，同一种控件在哪里都是同样的手感。 - **三个独立模块**：任务栏、桌面小组件和台前调度可以分别打开，只用其中一个也行。 - **中英文界面**：设置中心的“系统 → 语言”可选择简体中文、English，或跟随 Windows；栏、面板、菜单、通知、小组件和设置中心一起切换。语言文案在 `locales/` 下，每门语言一个 JSON 文件；没有翻译的词条回退英文。 - **干净**：不向系统进程注入代码，不改系统文件，不装服务，不需要管理员权限。退出后，Windows 自己的任务栏照常回来。 ## 功能 ### 液态与磨砂

玻璃会折射背后的画面，边缘带一点高光和色散。喜欢通透，用液态（左）；喜欢安静，用磨砂（右）。透明度、模糊和折射强度也可以在设置中心里自己调。玻璃上的文字会跟着背后的明暗自动换成深色或浅色。 ### 任务栏

- 悬浮在屏幕底部的胶囊形玻璃栏。指针划过时，图标像波浪一样放大，停一下会浮出应用名称。 - 指针停在打开的应用上，会显示它每个窗口的实时预览，可以直接切换或关闭。 - 右键图标和 Windows 任务栏一样，列出程序自己的跳转列表：已固定和最近的文件、文件夹、工作区，以及程序提供的任务（如浏览器的新窗口、无痕窗口）；还可以以管理员身份运行、查看属性。设置中心里可以关掉，恢复简单的菜单。 - 固定的应用可以拖动排序；前台应用全屏或最大化时，栏会让开（也可以设成常驻或一直隐藏）。游戏、视频等铺满整个屏幕的应用在前台时，指针碰到底边也不会唤出任务栏，和 Windows 任务栏一样，不会把全屏游戏挤回桌面。打开后，Win + 1…9 可以直接打开栏上的应用。 - 多显示器：在另一块屏幕底边停留即可唤出 Dock；也可固定到主屏、指定屏幕，或在所有屏幕显示任务栏。在设置中心的“显示器”页可选择任务栏应用显示在所有屏幕、主屏和窗口所在屏、或仅窗口所在屏，并调整跨屏停留时间。 - 小组件与台前调度可单独选择桌面显示器。目标屏幕断开时临时回到主屏，重新连接后自动恢复。 ### 开始菜单
点栏左侧的 Windows 徽标打开，也可以设成按 Win 键打开。Windows 开始菜单里固定的应用照常在这里；搜索框旁的同步按钮可以随时把 Windows 开始菜单的固定应用、以及“所有应用”里的文件夹连同其中的应用一起同步过来；图标可以拖动换位置，拖到另一个图标上就建成文件夹，可以命名。菜单有小、中、大、超大四档（对应设置 `small`/`medium`/`large`/`xlarge`），图标大小也可独立设置。打开后不用点搜索框，直接打字就能搜索应用和文件夹，也能按拼音首字母搜（wx 找到微信）；“全部应用”按 A–Z 排列，左侧字母条可以快速跳转。右键应用可以以管理员身份运行、打开文件所在的位置，不想看到的应用也可以右键隐藏。下面一条是账户、网络、音量、电量和电源；设置中心里可以选菜单大小，也可以去掉其中的托盘或状态按钮。 ### 状态圆环与控制中心

栏的右侧只有一个圆环，代替一排电池、网络和音量图标。外圈是电量，充电时开口处有一道闪电；中间是 Wi‑Fi。调音量或亮度时，圆环变成对应的刻度，1.5 秒后自己回到电量和 Wi‑Fi。在圆环上滚动滚轮可以直接调音量。习惯 Windows 的样子，也可以换成并排的网络、音量、电池三个图标。
点圆环打开控制中心：Wi‑Fi、蓝牙、电池、投屏、台前调度、显示器亮度、声音和输出设备，还能分别调各个应用的音量。点铃铛打开通知：新消息叠成一摞，点一下展开成列表。点时钟打开带农历和节日的日历。 设置中心的“通知 → 通知位置”可选择“跟随任务栏”（默认）或主屏四角（左上、右上、左下、右下）。屏幕角落模式下，新通知从屏幕边缘滑入，已有通知平滑让位；通知较多时可滚动查看，点击铃铛打开的通知中心也会在该角落展开。 ### 桌面小组件

时钟、数字时钟、日历（带农历）、天气、电池、蓝牙设备、网络、系统监视、备忘录、提醒事项和照片，十一类小组件，三种尺寸。中号的时钟和数字时钟会显示几座城市的时间，右键“更改城市…”可以逐个换成其他城市。拖到哪里都会吸附到网格上；指针移上去，下角会出现一段弧形握把，拖动它就能改变大小。小组件平时在所有窗口下面，按 Win + D 显示桌面时浮到最上。

三种材质可选：**跟随任务栏**的透明玻璃；把玻璃调暗、文字全白的**暮色**；不透明、带原本颜色的**原色**。 ### 台前调度
正在用的应用留在屏幕中间，其余应用收到一侧，窗口画面斜立成一列，每个窗口一张卡片，同一个应用的几个窗口也分开放。指针移上去，窗口转正并稍稍放大；点一下就换到前面，按住 Shift 点按可以把几个应用组成一组。侧边可以一直显示（压在侧边上的窗口来到前台时会自动挪到旁边；窗口最大化时侧边让开，指针碰到屏幕边缘再滑出），也可以只在指针碰到屏幕边缘时滑出。打开“窗口最小化到台前调度”后，最小化前面的应用，它的窗口画面会直接飞进侧边，不再缩到任务栏。设置中心里可以列出不参与台前调度的应用（默认只包含 Windows 系统截图工具），它

content.readme: # Gears of War Native - PC ports of Gears of War, Gears of War 2, Gears of War 3 and Gears of War: Judgment Hello all, I'm Shagg. These are my personal **native Windows versions** of the four Xbox 360 Gears of War games, made by static recompilation, with a launcher called **COGBox** that sets up your own copy of each game and starts it. This franchise is one of my favourites, so the project is near and dear to my heart. **Fully playable** with a few hiccups - if you hit one, please send a problem report (see below). **COGBox is back on GitHub!** This is our home again, and we're keeping [GitLab](https://gitlab.com/shagg88/cogbox) as a full backup with the same releases. **[Download the latest release](https://github.com/Shagg88/COGBox/releases)** · You need your own copy of each game and its title update. No game files are included, ever. **Online multiplayer is here (0.6.0):** play Gears of War online with friends again, peer to peer through COGBox's own matchmaking - no Xbox Live needed. Off until you turn it on in the launcher's Social tab. **[Join the COGBox Discord](https://discord.gg/Y6qGbzBKQZ)** - find people to play with, get help, share feedback. COGBox is on RecompLauncher, the free home for recompiled PC games. Get it straight from its developer: https://recomplauncher.com/game/cogbox > An unofficial fan project, not affiliated with Microsoft, Epic Games or The Coalition. "Gears of War", "Xbox" and > "Xbox 360" are trademarks of Microsoft. --- ## The games | Game | Tested disc | Tested title update | Status | |---|---|---|---| | Gears of War | Game version 0.0.0.1 | Title Update 5 (version 0.0.5.1) | Playable | | Gears of War 2 | US disc, game version 0.0.0.5 | Title Update 6 (version 0.0.6.5) | Every chapter plays in testing | | Gears of War 3 | Game version 0.0.0.11 | Title Update 6 (version 0.0.6.11) | Playable | | Gears of War: Judgment | Game version 0.0.0.9 | Title Update 4 (version 0.0.4.9) | Playable | Title updates are required; disc-only copies aren't supported. The versions are the ones the game itself reports (with the title update applied, the third number is the update's). Players have also reported other copies working, most likely other regions' releases: Gears of War, 2 copies of the disc; Gears of War 2, 1 of the title update; Gears of War 3, 5 of the title update; Judgment, 1 of the disc and 4 of the title update. COGBox checks your copy when you add it: a tested or reported copy is accepted as it is, any other copy is marked "untested" - it may work, but please try a tested one before reporting a problem. Each game's page in the launcher shows the same versions. ## Features The games' Xbox 360 code is translated ahead of time into ordinary Windows programs - no emulator runs while you play - and our own renderer draws every frame on Direct3D 12 (or Vulkan). - **Any resolution** up to 5K, or matched to your monitor, with real extra detail; **ultrawide** up to 48:9 (three screens) and **HDR10**. - **Modern lighting extras** (off by default): modern ambient occlusion (XeGTAO; one Default / On switch), and experimental PCSS soft shadows (Gears 3 and Judgment) and screen-space indirect lighting. - **Upscaling and anti-aliasing:** SMAA, AMD FSR and NVIDIA DLSS (experimental). - **High frame rates:** the 30 fps limit lifted, frame-rate caps from 30 to 180 (and 40 / 45 for the Steam Deck), and frame generation (AMD FSR, NVIDIA DLSS on RTX 40/50; experimental). - **Lower input lag:** NVIDIA Reflex and AMD Anti-Lag 2 where your GPU has them. - **Keyboard and mouse** or **Xbox / PlayStation controllers**, with button prompts that follow what you use, and DualSense adaptive triggers in all four games (experimental, off by default). - **Split-screen co-op** in all four games, and **System Link** LAN co-op (experimental). - **Online multiplayer** (0.6.0, off by default): peer to peer through COGBox's own matchmaking. - **Insane from the start**, **achievements** in all four games, chapter select, and an **in-game menu** (Back + Start, or F1) to change settings or quit. - **DLC and mods**, every language your copy has, and screenshots with **\\**. ## What you need - **Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit** (or Linux / Steam Deck through Proton, or a Mac with Apple Silicon through CrossOver - both experimental). - **A CPU with AVX2** (roughly 2013 or newer) and **a DirectX 12 graphics card** (under Proton: a graphics driver with Vulkan 1.3, such as a recent Mesa or NVIDIA driver). - **Your own copy of each game** - a disc image (.iso), a Games on Demand copy or the disc's extracted files - and its **title update**, copied from your console's `Content\0000000000000000\\000B0000\` folder (Gears of War `4D5307D5`, Gears 2 `4D53082D`, Gears 3 `4D5308AB`, Judgment `4D530A26`). - About 8-16 GB

content.readme: # Project ReLink **Zelda OOT Remake Recomp.** An unofficial static recompilation of *The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time* (the Switch 2 remake) into a native Windows game: the game's code is translated to PC code and compiled on your machine, with no emulator. [Français plus bas](#français) **Discord:** [join the Project ReLink server](https://discord.gg/RFNUtCQk8j) to ask questions, get help and follow new versions. Bugs are still best reported as [issues](https://github.com/pixl27/ProjectReLink/issues) with `relink_log.txt` attached, so they don't get lost. ![The Project ReLink launcher](docs/launcher.png) **No game files are in this repository.** ReLink builds the game on your PC from your own copy. ## The game version you need ReLink works with **one version of the game**: the Switch 2 remake with its update installed. | | | |---|---| | Program | `0400486024DEC000` | | Update | v131072 | | Build | `e0f3ccfa` | Other versions do not work: the launcher checks your copy and says so before it installs anything. Your copy is either a `.nup` file, or the game's `romfs` and `exefs` folders. ## Install and play 1. Download `ReLink-Setup.exe` from the [latest release](https://github.com/pixl27/ProjectReLink/releases/latest). 2. Run it. It downloads ReLink and its tools (about 310 MB), checks them and opens the launcher. Nothing else to install: ReLink brings its own compiler and Python. 3. Pick your copy of the game. The launcher looks for `.nup` files in Downloads, Desktop and Documents; you can also choose one, drop it on the window, or give the `romfs` and `exefs` folders. 4. Press **Install**. It takes 10 to 45 minutes depending on your CPU; you can keep using the PC. 5. Press **Play**. The desktop and Start menu shortcuts open the launcher from then on. **With RecompLauncher.** Each release also has `ProjectReLink--Windows-x64.zip`, the same tools in one file, with a `recomplauncher.json` that lets [RecompLauncher](https://recomplauncher.com) install ReLink, ask for your copy (the same version as above), build the game in the same way and start it. Its settings page writes the game's own `relink_options.ini`; the frame rate goes in `relink_env.txt` beside it. The first start is long, once (about 16 minutes on our PC): the game prepares its shaders, builds its graphics pipelines for your driver's cache and makes the compute pipelines play is known to use, with a progress screen. It does that part again after a graphics driver update, so that the first visit of a place does not stutter while the driver compiles, and after an update of ReLink that changes the renderer's shader code or state (0.6.3 is one). Since 0.7.6 every PC starts the same way, whatever its RAM. A PC that ran an earlier version with 20 GB of RAM or more has a pipeline cache file in the game folder, `mkw_vk_pipelines.bin` (800 MB and more), that nothing reads any more: since 0.7.8 the game deletes it at its first start, unless `RX_VK_LEAN_PIPELINES=0` in `relink_env.txt` brings back the older start, which uses it. ![Installing](docs/install.png) ![The first start: the night ends as the game gets ready](docs/loading.png) ### What your PC needs - 64-bit Windows 10 or 11, and a CPU with AVX2. - A graphics card with Vulkan 1.3 and mesh shaders, with an up-to-date driver: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 20 series or newer, AMD Radeon RX 6000 series or newer, Intel Arc. We only tested on NVIDIA. Since 0.7.9 a card without mesh shaders (GeForce GTX 10 series) gets a picture too, as an experiment: about half the frame rate, and some large rocks missing. - 8 GB of video memory recommended, 16 GB of RAM or more. - About 60 GB free while it installs, and an internet connection for the download. ### Updating The launcher says when a new release is out. **Update** downloads only what changed and builds the game again in the same folder, from the game files the folder keeps: your `.nup` is not needed again. Saves (`user`), settings and mods are kept. ### Where the files go - The game: the folder you choose (`Games\ReLink` in your user folder by default). Your copy is never changed. - ReLink itself: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ReLink`. The build files (about 4 GB) are deleted once the game is ready. - To uninstall: delete the game folder, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ReLink` and the shortcuts. ## Settings The launcher sets the display (full screen, 3D render resolution, upscaling, sharpness, ultrawide), the smoothness (60 frames a second or unlocked, frame generation), the game's language and the controls. # idrive-apps

Apps for the iDrive 7 head unit of a BMW, installed from the
[mgu Store](https://github.com/robertnisipeanu/mgu-store).

## Maps on cluster

Shows your phone's navigation map on the instrument cluster: CarPlay (Waze,
Apple Maps or Google Maps) or Android Auto (Google Maps). It can also show it
on the head-up display (experimental).

![The map on the cluster](docs/hud/cluster-map.jpg)

**Install:** in the Store, install **Maps on cluster** from the
`robertnisipeanu/idrive-apps` source (add the source if your Store doesn't
list it). Restart the head unit when the Store asks, and
in the car's settings set **Instrument cluster > Central display area** to
**Map view**. On a
supported car the map turns on by itself; you don't need to press anything
in the app.

Settings, what to do if the map doesn't show, and how to send logs:
[Maps on cluster](apps/robertn_waze_cluster/README.md).

### On the head-up display

Choose **HUD (experimental)** or **Cluster and HUD (experimental)** in the
app's **Show on**. You can set the map's size and position on the HUD. At
night the map's background is black, so only the roads, route and labels
show. Photos from a 2021 X5 xDrive45e (G05); street names blurred.

![The HUD map while driving](docs/hud/hud-on-the-road.jpg)

*The HUD map while driving. (The panel at the bottom right, battery power
and temperatures, is a separate app.)*

| Waze's grey-blue night background on the HUD | The background made black, which the HUD shows as nothing |
|---|---|
| ![Before](docs/hud/hud-before-black-background.jpg) | ![After](docs/hud/hud-night.jpg) |

## For developers

| Path | |
|---|---|
| [`native/cluster-render`](native/cluster-render) | the cluster renderer: one service that draws every app's layers on the instrument cluster and the HUD, on iDrive 7 and iDrive 8 |
| [`native/waze-on-cluster`](native/waze-on-cluster) | the CarPlay map (Waze, Apple Maps or Google Maps), or Android Auto's, on the instrument cluster, drawn through cluster-render |
| [`apps/robertn_waze_cluster`](apps/robertn_waze_cluster) | the iDrive app for it: where the map shows, the patches' status and buttons, Logs |
| [`release`](release) | builds and publishes the Store catalog |
| `tools` | `oap_pack.js`, `oap_link.js`: pack the app |

Installing the app installs what it requires first: `mgu-deploy` from
mgu-store, then `cluster-render` and `waze-on-cluster` from here. The
`waze-on-cluster` install hook writes the CarPlay patch, and the Android Auto
patch on a car that supports it; one head-unit start activates them. The
Store removes them in the reverse order: the app, then the tool, then the
renderer.

### Build

```sh
make -C native/cluster-render test test-x86 target    # host tests; the unit's toolchain and binary (Docker)
make -C native/waze-on-cluster test test-x86 target
node apps/robertn_waze_cluster/tools/test_control.js
node apps/robertn_waze_cluster/tools/test_page.js
node apps/robertn_waze_cluster/tools/test_i18n.js
node release/test/release_test.js
node release/release.js check                         # reproducible artifacts
```

Each folder's README has the details; [`release/README.md`](release/README.md)
covers versions, the catalog and publishing. Before opening a pull request,
read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md): the release sets versions.

### License

GPL-3.0-or-later ([`LICENSE`](LICENSE)), unless a file's SPDX header says
otherwise. What apps compile in or copy from cluster-render, its `include/`,
`client/`, `kit/`, `js/cluster_render_client.js` and `PROTOCOL.md`, is
MPL-2.0 ([`LICENSES/MPL-2.0.txt`](LICENSES/MPL-2.0.txt)). Third-party files
keep their own licenses: the RAMSES and vsomeip interfaces in cluster-render
(MPL-2.0), the Intel Media SDK headers in waze-on-cluster (MIT), Project
Nayuki's QR code generator in robertn_waze_cluster (MIT).

Orchid

A very experimental Switch 2 emulator. Orchid started from Eglantine and has grown into its own project, with fixes aimed at Mario Tennis Fever first, plus the shader, kernel and graphics work other games need.

> [!NOTE] > Orchid is an independent project. Problems with these builds are not caused by the Eglantine > or Eden developers, so please do not report them there.

Project scope | Branches and builds | What Orchid adds | Performance | Download | Build it yourself | Documentation | License

Orchid opens NXFormat (`.nx`) game archives directly from the file picker or a game directory. The reader comes from [nxformat](https://github.com/fab918/nxformat), with the loader adapted from [Lichii](https://github.com/sheepbun/Lichii/tree/2f0c8df47af2a4de0477839ed54c80b260377ea8). ## Project scope Orchid's support and development focus is on demonstrably improving these games: - Mario Tennis Fever - Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment - Pokémon Pokopia - Star Fox - Super Mario Bros. content.readme: # Luciole A native Wayland file manager built to stay smooth: quick to start, fluid when scrolling through large folders, and previews that never block the window. It offers grid, list and Miller column views, tabs, split view and rich file previews, and runs on any Wayland compositor. It also serves as the Open and Save file picker for other applications through xdg-desktop-portal. It pairs naturally with [Noctalia](https://github.com/noctalia-dev/noctalia) and [Umbriel](https://github.com/noctalia-dev/umbriel). Under the hood: C++23, direct Wayland and OpenGL ES, with no Qt or GTK. > [!IMPORTANT] > Luciole is young and actively evolving. It is usable today, but settings, shortcuts and behavior may change between releases, and rough edges remain. ## Why Luciole? We wanted a file manager that responds as fast as we can move. Folders with thousands of files should open and scroll without a stutter, thumbnails should fill in as you go instead of freezing the view, and a second window should not cost a second application. That shaped how Luciole is built: - **GPU rendering:** the interface draws directly through OpenGL ES, so scrolling, zooming and resizing stay fluid even with many thumbnails on screen. - **Nothing blocks the window:** folder listing, file operations and thumbnail decoding run in the background, and image decoding happens in sandboxed helper processes. - **One process, many windows:** every window shares a single process, so extra windows and tabs stay light on memory. - **Shared caches:** thumbnails are reused from the standard freedesktop cache, so folders you have already browsed in other file managers appear instantly. It also aims to be complete enough for everyday work with archives, network shares and large photo folders, while staying consistent with the rest of the Noctalia family. To understand the values and philosophy guiding the project, read our [ethos](https://noctalia.dev/ethos). ## Features - **Browsing:** grid, list and optional Miller columns, with tabs, separate windows, split view, adjustable zoom and sortable detail columns - **Navigation and search:** clickable breadcrumbs, path completion, recursive filename search and instant filtering of the current folder - **Thumbnails and previews:** images, video, text and PDF pages, plus file and media metadata - **File operations:** copy, move, links, batch rename, folder merging, conflict choices, Trash and restoration, with [Undo and Redo](docs/user/file-operations.md#undo-and-redo) - **Archives:** browse, create and extract, with password prompts for [encrypted formats](docs/user/file-operations.md#archives) - **Places:** an adaptive sidebar with shared bookmarks, mounted drives, LUKS unlock prompts and optional folder trees - **File picker:** a [portal backend](docs/user/installation.md#use-luciole-as-the-file-picker) that provides Luciole's Open and Save dialogs for applications using the FileChooser portal; [xdg-desktop-portal-umbriel](https://github.com/noctalia-dev/xdg-desktop-portal-umbriel) selects it automatically when installed, and other desktops can enable it in `portals.conf` - **Desktop integration:** SFTP, SMB and WebDAV locations, Open With, terminal actions and [custom scripts](docs/user/scripts.md) - **Configuration:** built-in settings, live-reloaded TOML, icon themes and configurable colors ## Install and run See the [installation guide](docs/user/installation.md) for Arch Linux, Fedora, Debian and Ubuntu packages, source builds and Nix. Then launch Luciole from your application menu, or from a terminal: ```sh luciole luciole ~/Downloads ``` ## Configuration Open Settings with Ctrl+, or from the main menu; changes apply immediately. For manual configuration, use `~/.config/luciole/config.toml`. The [configuration guide](docs/user/configuration.md)

This is an early alpha. Video, audio, controller input, and saves have been confirmed working. Compatibility and performance will vary between games. The current release is **v1.000.003** (a pre-release). ## Source code The complete EglantinePS5 source is in this repository: the PS5 frontend and launcher in `headless/`, and the build and packaging tools in `tools/`. To build it yourself, run `make` on Linux (Ubuntu 26.04; WSL works). It fetches every dependency at its pinned revision and writes the release files to `dist/`; `make help` lists the other targets. See the [setup guide and current limitations](docs/MULTIPLAYER.md) and the [validation status](docs/MULTIPLAYER_IMPLEMENTATION.md); Tailscale forwarding is not yet qualified. ## Linux testing on a BC250 `make linux-appimage JOBS=4` builds a Linux Qt/SDL AppImage with separate debug symbols. `make linux-install` deploys it over SSH to `BC250_HOST` (default `bazzite@192.168.0.167`) using a separate test profile. See [Linux build and capture instructions](tools/linux/README.txt) for dependencies, debugging tools, and the differences from the PS5 frontend. ## Project foundation > [!IMPORTANT] > **Built on the [PS5 Native App Boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate), the same native foundation used by ProsperoLight.** > It provides the native PS5 application structure, runtime, packaging, and homebrew deployment foundation. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Graphics are powered by [ps5-opengl](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-opengl).** > This OpenGL implementation provides the native PS5 rendering layer used by the Eden graphics backend. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Vulkan is powered by Mihawk's [PS5 Mesa](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa) and [PS5 Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan).** > Mihawk's Mesa/RADV driver for the PS5 runs EglantinePS5's Vulkan renderer. # Venture **A Meta Quest emulator for PC VR.** Play the Meta Quest games you own on your PC headset, at full PC speed and resolution.
No virtual machine. Free and open source. [**Download**](https://github.com/Villagers654/Venture/releases/latest) · [Website](https://venture-emu.org/) · [Report an issue](https://github.com/Villagers654/Venture/issues) · [Discord](https://discord.gg/Ey9hHszvwa)
## Why Venture - **Fast.** Venture is by far the fastest way to play Quest games on PC, with steady frame times. - **Compatible.** Runs all 25 games we tested; see the [compatibility wiki](https://github.com/Villagers654/Venture/wiki/Compatibility). The next best runs 7. - **Straight to your hardware.** Every game runs as an ordinary PC process that renders on your GPU and talks to your headset through OpenXR. - **Simple.** Sign in with Meta, install, press Play. Your games can show up in your Steam library too. ### Install and play 1. Download `Venture-windows64-setup.exe` from [Releases](https://github.com/Villagers654/Venture/releases/latest) and run it. On Linux, install the package for your distribution (`.deb`, `.rpm`, AUR `venture-bin`, AppImage or Flatpak), or extract the `.tar.gz` anywhere. 2. Start Venture and choose Sign in with Meta and use the account that owns your Quest games. If Meta's sign-in window doesn't open, or you'd rather use your own browser, choose **Sign in manually** under it. 3. Pick a game in your library and choose **Install**. 4. Start your headset's runtime, then choose **Play**. ### Games from somewhere else The **Import** page adds games that aren't in your Meta library: - **From a headset:** connect a Quest with developer mode on (USB, or Wi-Fi debugging) and choose **Scan headset**. Nothing on the headset is changed. - **From this computer:** choose or drop an APK, a ZIP, or a folder with the APK and its data. ### Play from Steam Turn on **Add games to Steam** in Settings. Installed games appear in Steam and SteamVR the next time Steam starts. ### Mods Mods that replace a game's expansion file (OBB), such as RE4 VR Definitive Edition, go in the game's mods folder: open the game in your library and choose **Open folder** next to **Mods**, then put the mod's file there under the same name as the installed file (for example `main.203.com.Armature.VR4.obb`). It is used from the next launch; your installation is not changed, and deleting the file goes back to the original. ### Mixed reality (passthrough) Games that use Quest passthrough show your surroundings when your VR runtime or headset can: through the runtime's own passthrough (`XR_FB_passthrough` or `XR_HTC_passthrough`), its see-through blend mode, the headset's cameras through SteamVR, or (for now) the Steam Link native passthrough companion. A color key for streaming tools that key a color can be chosen instead. It is on by default; **Settings → Runtime → Passthrough (mixed reality)** keeps every game in VR. See [Mixed Reality](https://github.com/Villagers654/Venture/wiki/Mixed-Reality) on the wiki for known setups. ### Something wrong? If a game crashes, click **Report issue** on the banner that appears. Otherwise, use **Upload debug report** in Settings. Either way, Venture collects the launcher and game logs from your last launch into one debug report, uploads it as an unlisted paste that expires after 90 days, and gives you a link to copy. If the upload fails, attach the report file instead (**Show file**). The report starts with what happened in the last run and its likely cause; `venture-cli report [GAME] --upload` writes the same from a terminal. [Open an issue](https://github.com/Villagers654/Venture/issues/new/choose) with the game, what happened, how to make it happen again and the debug report link. To watch a game's output live, turn on **Show runtime console** in Settings. For help or to chat, join the [Discord](https://discord.gg/Ey9hHszvwa). ### Build (Windows) ```sh python tools/bootstrap.py --jdk --angle # pinned toolchain, JDK and ANGLE into .deps/ .deps/cmake/bin/cmake --preset windows-release .deps/cmake/bin/cmake --build --preset windows-release ``` ### Build (Linux) ```sh python3 tools/bootstrap.py --jdk # pinned CMake, Ninja and JDK into .deps/ .deps/cmake/bin/cmake --preset linux-release .deps/cmake/bin/cmake --build

# ESP32 AirPlay 2 Surround Gateway **Wireless 5.1 / 7.1 surround sound from an Apple TV, built from low-cost ESP32-S3 boards: one Gateway, and one board per speaker.** The Apple TV sees **one AirPlay 2 speaker: the Gateway**. The Gateway takes the complete surround stream and passes it on, unchanged, to up to **eight speaker boards** over your Wi-Fi. Every speaker decodes **only its own channel** (Front Left, Centre, Subwoofer, Rear Right, …) and plays it through any amplifier and speaker you like. All speakers share one clock taken from the Wi-Fi access point itself, so they play each sample at the same moment. No cables between the speakers, no AV receiver, one web page for the whole system. - 🎬 **5.1 and 7.1 AAC** (Apple Music Dolby Atmos, films and series from the Apple TV apps). - 🎵 **Stereo** too: ALAC 44.1 kHz/16-bit and **lossless 48 kHz/24-bit**, AAC 44.1 / 48 kHz, from any AirPlay 2 sender. A stereo song plays on the front pair and the subwoofer, as on an AV receiver. - 📡 **One AirPlay target.** You pick the Gateway, not eight speakers. Pairing, RTSP and the Apple TV's clock are handled once, by the Gateway. - 🏠 **Apple Home (HomeKit)** pairing, artwork, playback and volume controls for the whole surround system as one speaker. - ⏱️ **Microsecond clock alignment** between speakers through the access point's beacon timer (TSF). No extra hardware, no cables. - 🎤 **Room calibration** with an optional INMP441 microphone on the Gateway: distance, delay and level of every speaker measured from your seat, applied with one click. - 📈 **Room EQ** with the same microphone: each speaker's frequency response measured from your seat and corrected with its own EQ, with settings like REW's. - 📻 **Web radio** on the Gateway: stations of your country, a search, your favourites or any stream address (MP3 or AAC over HTTP / HTTPS), played on all speakers like an AirPlay stream. content.readme:
# Super Mario All-Stars — PC Port

A native Windows and Android version of *Super Mario All-Stars* (SNES) with a launcher, true widescreen,
re-anchored HUDs, display options, cheats, level select, achievements, a sound test and a music
player. **It contains no game data: it runs from your own ROM**
(`Super Mario All-Stars (USA).sfc`, CRC32 `925637C7`); no game starts without it.

## Building
Requirements: Windows 10/11, Visual Studio 2022 (C++ workload) and CMake 3.20+.
No other libraries are needed (Direct3D 11, Direct2D, XAudio2, XInput and
DirectInput come with Windows).

```
build.bat
```
The program is written to `build\Release\SuperMarioAllStars.exe`.

### Android
The same code builds for Android (`android/`), as the Mickey & Donald Collection's does: SDL2 2.32.10
compiled from source for the window, sound and controllers, OpenGL ES 3.0 for the picture. You need the
Android SDK with NDK 28.2 and CMake 3.31.6 (both from the SDK manager) and JDK 17 or later. The SDL2 source
belongs in `third_party/SDL2-2.32.10-src` (`android/fetch_sdl.ps1` downloads and checks it), then:

```
cd android
gradlew assembleDebug
```
The APK ends up in `android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/` (64-bit ARM phones and tablets, Android 6.0 or
later, and the x86_64 emulator). Release builds are signed when `android/keystore.properties` names a
keystore (`storeFile`, `storePassword`, `keyAlias`, `keyPassword`), as the Disney collection's are.

## Running
Put the ROM next to the executable, in a `roms` folder beside it, or in any parent folder up to
three levels up; the location is remembered in `rompath.txt`. Without it the launcher's cards say
*ROM not found* and what is needed, and a ROM copied in while the launcher is open is picked up
within a second. Another version or dump of All-Stars runs too, its file name shown in amber on the
cards: widescreen, cheats and the level select are tuned for the USA version.

To start a game directly, give `SuperMarioAllStars.exe` the argument `--game smb1`, `--game smbll`,
`--game smb2` or `--game smb3` (for example in a shortcut).

Battery saves go to `saves\smas.srm`, save states to `saves\`,
screenshots to `screenshots\`, settings to `smas_port.ini`. Files are written in full before
they replace the old ones, so a full disk can't leave a truncated save (you are told the save
failed instead). Save states carry a checksum: a damaged one is refused rather than loaded. They
also keep the widescreen state, so a state loads exactly as it was saved, and one saved at a
narrower width (or by an older version) brings in the enemies of the wider view. If the graphics
driver resets (a driver update or crash), the picture comes back by itself and the game keeps
running.

## On Android
Install the APK (Android asks you to allow installing apps from the place you opened it). On the first
start the launcher's card says *ROM not found*: tap it, pick `Super Mario All-Stars (USA).sfc` (or a
`.smc`) in the file picker, and it is copied into the app. A ROM can also be put in the app's folder
`Android/data/com.darhkfox.allstars/files` (or a `roms` folder there) with a computer.

- **Touch:** an SNES pad over the game: the D-pad bottom left, A B X Y bottom right, L and R at the
  sides, Select and Start bottom centre, Menu top left, and (when they're switched on and achievements
  are off) rewind and fast forward top right. Tap a game's card to choose it, tap it again to play; in
  the menus tap a row to use it, drag to scroll, and the button top right goes back.
- **Controllers and keyboards** work as on Windows (the same bindings); the on-screen controls hide
  while one is in use (*Options → Controls → On-Screen Controls*: While Touching, Always or Never, and
  their opacity).
- **Back** opens and closes the menu, as Esc does.
- The picture fills the screen (*Aspect Ratio: Auto*), with the same filters and colour settings. The
  window settings, VSync, Black Frame Insertion, High Frame Rate and slang shaders are Windows only.
- Saves, states and settings are kept in the app's own storage; screenshots go to
  `Android/data/com.darhkfox.allstars/files/screenshots`. Leaving the app saves the game's progress.

## Launcher
The program opens on a launcher, laid out like the Mickey & Donald Collection's, over a night-blue
sky with twinkling stars and a checkerboard floor after the All-Stars title screen. By default it
shows one **Super Mario All-Stars** card with a live preview of the cartridge's title: choosing it
starts the cartridge as it is, at its own title and game select (`--game allstars` starts it
directly). Below are buttons for **Options**, **Achievements**, **Music Player**, **Credits** and
**Quit**.

*Options → Launcher Shows → The Four Games* gives one card per game instead (Super Mario Bros., The
Lost Levels, Super Mario Bros. 2, Super Mario Bros. 3), each with a live attract-mode preview of that
game and the chosen card's sound playing. Each preview is its own console run through the All-Stars
